method: eth_estimateGas, min of 3 runs. Fixed costs (21000 intrinsic, calldata, router dispatch, uncached Stylus module init) removed two independent ways.

stylus_rust_p256.note: p256 crate (RustCrypto) compiled to WASM, verify_prehash only. No SHA-256, no parsing, no storage, no outbound call.

isolationCrossCheck.note: x2-x1 cancels every fixed cost including per-call WASM init; both methods agree, so ~362k is the real compute cost.

rip7212_precompile.note: RIP-7212 secp256r1 precompile is LIVE on Arbitrum Sepolia. Not a published figure -- measured here against the same real signature.

solidity_published_reference.note: NOT measured here. Published figures for hand-rolled Solidity P-256 verifiers (e.g. Daimo p256-verifier ~330k, FreshCryptoLib ~200k). /solidity was never built.

conclusion.stylusVsSolidity: Stylus Rust p256 at ~362k gas is SLOWER than published Solidity verifiers at 200k-330k. The project's premise that Rust on Stylus would be dramatically cheaper is NOT supported by measurement.
conclusion.precompileVsBoth: The RIP-7212 precompile at ~7.2k gas is roughly 50x cheaper than the Stylus implementation and ~30-45x cheaper than Solidity verifiers.
conclusion.premiseCorrection: CLAUDE.md states the EVM has NO precompile for secp256r1. That is no longer true on Arbitrum: RIP-7212 is live at 0x100 on Arbitrum Sepolia and verified the real fixture signature.
